scope: mechanism investigation, expansion attempt, and implementation-variant decision; no src/ changes

mechanism.verdict: Tier-2/3 safety indexes are re-extracted from the directly shadowed, visible parent checkpoint node; they are not an engine-side inheritance of the parent block's original index or source coverage.

evidence.finding: A live checkpoint seq is resolved to its kernel block ref, which makes the kernel create a distillation block.

After each model-written summary, ARC calls buildModelSummarySafetyIndex(agent, shadowed) and persists model summary plus appendix as one replacement user message. For tier 2/3, shadowed is the parent checkpoint seq, so the appendix is built from that message rather than an expanded parent source list.
The index projects/extracts each supplied event text into bounded previews, structured matches, distinctive lines, and signals. It has no parent-block argument and no recursive lookup.
Recursive parent expansion exists only for recovery (expandShadowedSeqs); the compression path above does not use it.
decompress is the consumer of recursive recovery; it returns expanded originals, confirming that source inheritance is retrieval-only.

mechanism.modelVisibleSurface: The next model sees the durable checkpoint user message: its model-authored summary followed by the [ARC MODEL-CHECKPOINT SAFETY INDEX — REVERSIBLE EXTRACTIVE APPENDIX]. It does not receive a separate hidden parent-source/index channel. Because tier 2/3 index construction re-extracts that whole checkpoint text, selected parent-index strings can survive, but this is lossy textual re-extraction, not provenance-preserving inheritance.
mechanism.implication: An index-first implementation must explicitly refresh or carry effective-source evidence across tiers; merely retaining the current appended appendix does not guarantee source-level preservation.

expansion.protocol: First-round forced model-written tier-1→tier-2→tier-3 protocol reused; zh corpus is buildScript(..., { locale: 'zh' }) shared with RQ3. Experimental control was coreOverrides.protectedRecentMessages=0 and protectedRecentTokens=1 (production defaults 5 and 5000), with autoNudge and Governor disabled. This only made the forced source span eligible; it is not a production recommendation.

budget.reasonStopped: The live RPC runner was interrupted while sessions continued server-side. One completed chain used 16 calls and two partial sessions had already used 11 calls. Completing the six-chain plan would have required at least 107 calls on the observed path, exceeding the hard cap; the isolated dsh host was stopped.

observedButNonDecisionGrade.carrier: all 20 loose survivors were both model-summary and index-bearing at every tier
observedButNonDecisionGrade.interpretation: This operational observation is not pooled with RQ4 and does not satisfy the ≥3 seed × bilingual matrix: the interrupted queue altered timing, and tier-2 decompression's effective-source predicate missed one source event.

expansion.criterion: The required ≥2/3 seed × both-locale replication is not available. RQ4 index-first therefore remains unapproved for implementation on generalization evidence.

variants.design: At a tier boundary, inject the parent appendix as an explicitly labelled distillation input beside the parent summary.
variants.expectedEffect: May reduce model omission if prompt salience rather than visibility is the failure mode.
variants.risk: Current checkpoint text already contains the appendix, so this can duplicate tokens without fixing re-extraction loss.

variants.design: When landing tier 2/3, build the safety appendix from recursively expanded effective parent source seqs, not from the parent checkpoint node alone; retain parent provenance in the ledger.
variants.expectedEffect: Preserves the index carrier at source fidelity across layers while keeping model-written summaries unchanged.
variants.risk: Larger appendix and bounded-index truncation need a size gate; archive-instruction filtering must remain identical.

variants.design: Leave distillation unchanged, but rank the safety appendix ahead of model prose for search/retrieval and disclose it as archive data.
variants.expectedEffect: Improves recovery access, not model-summary tier retention.
variants.risk: Does not address telephone-game loss in the hot checkpoint.

variantDecision.recommended: B-effective-source-index-refresh, conditionally gated by a corrected six-chain rerun.
variantDecision.reason: The mechanism rules out hidden inheritance and shows A is largely duplicative; B directly removes the identified re-extraction boundary while preserving the existing model-written-summary and archive-safety contracts.
variantDecision.expectedBenefitEstimate: Directional, not yet measured: the first RQ4 pool had tier-3 model-summary strict retention 4/60 (6.7%) and 33/34 loose survivors index-bearing. B is expected to keep the appendix carrier near the observed 90%+ range across tier 3; no justified model-summary strict-retention percentage can be promised until the corrected bilingual matrix is run.

checks.npmRunCheck: pass before live attempt (158 tests, typecheck, build, public evidence verification)
